icd10_codes.description: Sprain of unspecified ligament of left ankle, initial encounter
Fall on same level, unspecified, initial encounter

dialogue:
[doctor] hi , {PATIENT_FIRST} . i'm doctor {DOCTOR_LAST} . what brings you in today ?
[patient] i twisted my ankle pretty bad on monday morning . it's the left one . it's swollen like a balloon .
[doctor] i'm sorry to hear that . tell me how it happened .
[patient] i drive a forklift on the night shift , and i'd come off a bad low . my sugar was like fifty two , and i was dizzy , so i got off the forklift to grab some juice from the break room . i stepped down off the dock and my foot just rolled under me .
[doctor] okay . so you were low on sugar at the time . did you pass out or hit your head when you fell ?
[patient] no , i did n't black out . i was just dizzy and shaky . i did n't hit my head , i caught myself on the railing .
[doctor] good . what did you do after you fell ?
[patient] i sat down on the dock , ate two glucose tabs , and then a coworker drove me home . i iced it that night .
[doctor] which coworker was that ?
[patient] {OTHER_FIRST} . he's always looking out for me .
[doctor] okay . how has your diabetes been overall ?
[patient] i've had type two for about nine years . i take glipizide every morning and i check my sugars four times a day . but the night shifts mess everything up , i eat at weird hours .
[doctor] i understand . how often are you having lows ?
[patient] maybe twice a month , more lately since they moved me to nights . i'd say one of them is really bad .
[doctor] i see . let's look at the ankle . is there pain on the outer side ?
[patient] yes , right here , on the outside . it hurts when i put weight on it .
[doctor] let me check . there's swelling and bruising over the lateral malleolus . can you wiggle your toes ?
[patient] yes . the toes move , but it hurts when i point my foot down .
[doctor] okay . your sensation is intact and your pulses are strong . there's no tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal . the drawer test is limited by the pain .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] we'll get an x-ray today . it's most likely a sprain , but i want to make sure there's no fracture .
[patient] okay .
[doctor] the x-ray shows no fracture , and the ankle is in good alignment . so i'm diagnosing a sprain of the ligaments on the outside of your ankle . here's the wrap and a walking boot for two weeks .
[patient] two weeks , and then i can go back to work ?
[doctor] i'd rather you not drive a forklift until you can bear full weight without pain . can your supervisor move you to light duty ?
[patient] maybe . i'll ask . i don't want to lose the night differential .
[doctor] the lows matter more right now . your last a one c was eight point four . you're taking the glipizide , and i want to add a continuous glucose monitor .
[patient] like a sensor on the arm ? my cousin has one .
[doctor] yes , it alerts you before the sugar drops . also , keep a glucose tab in your pocket on shift , and eat a snack at the start of your break .
[patient] okay . the washington guidelines say the sugar target is different for people like me ?
[doctor] that's a good question . the general target for most adults is an a one c under seven , but we can talk about something a bit looser given your lows .
[patient] okay , i'd like that .
[doctor] i'm also going to reduce your glipizide dose to five milligrams . and i'll check your kidney function today .
[patient] any side effects with the lower dose ?
[doctor] possibly more sugar swings , but the sensor should help . let's come back in four weeks to look at the sensor data .
[patient] will do . my wife will be happy about the sensor .
[doctor] good . any questions ?
[patient] just one . can i take a shower in the boot ?
[doctor] no , keep the boot dry and use a plastic bag . the wrap can come off at night .
[patient] okay . thanks , doctor .
[doctor] see you in four weeks . if your foot turns numb or cold , or the swelling gets worse , come in right away .
note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT

Left ankle pain and swelling after a fall during a hypoglycemic episode.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS

{PATIENT_FIRST} {PATIENT_LAST} is a {AGE}-year-old male with type 2 diabetes mellitus on glipizide who presents with left ankle pain and swelling following an inversion injury on {DATE_SPOKEN}. He works as a forklift operator on the night shift at a distribution center. He developed symptomatic hypoglycemia with a reported glucose of 52 mg/dL and dizziness, stepped down from the loading dock, and his left foot rolled under him. He caught himself on a railing and did not lose consciousness or strike his head. He sat, ingested glucose tablets, and was driven home by a coworker. He applied ice that evening.

He reports recurrent hypoglycemia about twice monthly, worse since transitioning to night shifts with irregular meals.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY

Type 2 diabetes mellitus, diagnosed in {YEAR}.

PHYSICAL EXAM

Left ankle: swelling and ecchymosis over the lateral malleolus with tenderness to palpation. Able to move toes; pain with plantarflexion. Neurovascularly intact distally. No tenderness over the base of the fifth metatarsal. Anterior drawer limited by pain.

RESULTS

Radiographs of the left ankle show no fracture and an intact mortise.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN

1. Sprain of the lateral ligaments of the left ankle, initial encounter, following a fall on the same level. No fracture. RICE protocol, lace-up ankle wrap, walking boot for two weeks, weight-bearing as tolerated. Advised against operating a forklift until he can bear full weight without pain; discussed light duty with supervisor.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus with recurrent hypoglycemia, most recent A1c 8.4%. Reduce glipizide to 5 mg daily. Start continuous glucose monitor. Glucose tablets to be carried on shift. Individualized A1c target discussed given hypoglycemia risk. Renal function to be checked.
3. Follow-up in four weeks for review of continuous glucose monitor data.
